[RFCS.24.2] **Replay delivers the input through the receiving rules.** A
replayer meeting an `ExternalAssert` must assert its `fact` as [RFCS.23.7]
receives a `FactExternal`, apply `ttl_ns` to the received fact as
[RFCS.6.2] applies a `FactAssert`'s, and bind the handles in `fact_ids`, in
order, to the facts that delivery asserts.

Replay starts each input from the working memory the original run had at that
point ([LFST.9.2.1]). So [RFCS.23.7]'s first rule, that a live fact equal to an
inlined copy is the same fact, resolves every reference to the fact it named
when recorded, whether that fact was an input or derived.

A recorded `ExternalAssert` was admitted when it was recorded ([RFCS.24.1]). So
a delivery that refuses, or that asserts a different number of facts than
`fact_ids` lists, is a replay that has not reproduced the run. The replayer must
stop with `DS_ERR_FS_DIVERGENCE`.

A halt that stops a delivery part-way ([NCBK.10.4]) is no refusal. `fact_ids`
lists the facts asserted before the delivery stopped, and a replay that stops at
the same fact has re-derived the recorded run's halt: the replayer **must** treat
it as an outcome ([RFCS.6.7]). A delivery a failed allocation stopped is not a
function of its input, so a replay that does not meet the failure asserts more
facts than `fact_ids` lists, and diverges.
